TWO1.question: Do teachers and mentors agree more about typical states than individual occasions?
TWO1.short: Do teachers and mentors agree more about typical states than individual occasions?
TWO1.prediction: Between-person agreement exceeds within-person agreement. A secondary marker asks whether within-person agreement is less than half the between-person value.
TWO1.source: Paired teaching diary, retained as tests only. R48 permits publication of the aggregate comparisons from this publicly obtainable source.
TWO1.sample: Rows give paired people and occasions. Within-person correlations use the repeated-person count.
TWO1.method: Whole-person bootstrap of teacher–mentor correlations. The difference and half-size contrasts use the same resampled people. The table covers every assessed quantity.
TWO1.basis: The ordering varies in precision across quantities. The table shows which difference intervals clear zero.
TWO1.limit: Averaging reduces noise. Agreement alone cannot establish which rater was correct.

GAT1.question: Does shared interest strengthen the association between partner ratings and a yes?
GAT1.short: Does shared interest strengthen the association between partner ratings and a yes?

GAT1.sample: Size counts raters. Observations count encounters.
GAT1.method: Within-rater logistic coefficient for attractiveness, ambition and intelligence averaged together, interacted with shared interest. Intervals resample whole raters.

UGM1.question: Do unexpected offers change responders’ feelings?
UGM1.short: Do unexpected offers change responders’ feelings?
UGM1.prediction: The offer gap adds information about valence, and surprises of either sign raise arousal.
UGM1.source: Heffner, Son and FeldmanHall, Study 1, [source study](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41562-021-01213-6). R48 permits publication of the aggregate comparisons from this publicly obtainable source.
UGM1.sample: Size counts contributing responders with within-person variation. Observations count fitted trials.
UGM1.method: Valence regressed on offer, difference from expectation and change from the preceding offer. Arousal fits use surprise magnitude separately by sign. Intervals resample whole players.
UGM1.basis: The gap interval includes zero and negative surprises do not have a clear positive arousal slope.
UGM1.limit: Within-player associations cannot establish which feature of an offer caused a feeling.
UGM1.headline: Valence, expectation gap
